gloss: to prostrate oneself; to crouch down on all fours; to grovel

definitions.gloss: to prostrate oneself; to crouch down on all fours; to grovel
definitions.explanation: To lower oneself flat against the ground or floor, putting hands and knees down. Used both literally (e.g., crawling, searching the floor) and figuratively for groveling or submitting abjectly. Compound of {這|は}う (to crawl) + つくばる (to crouch low).

examples.japanese: ⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{這|は}いつくばる。
examples.english: To get down flat on the floor.

examples.japanese: ⟦{落|お}とした→落とす：01246_otosu⟧⟦{指輪|ゆびわ}→指輪：01744_yubiwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}して→探す：00493_sagasu⟧{這|は}いつくばった。
examples.english: I got down on all fours looking for the ring I'd dropped.

examples.japanese: ⟦ミス→ミス：00285_misu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{謝|あやま}る→謝る：01177_ayamaru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{這|は}いつくばるようにして⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げた→下げる：00807_sageru⟧。
examples.english: To apologize for the mistake, he bowed his head before the boss as though prostrating himself.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{這|は}う→這う：00094_hau⟧ ("to crawl") + つくばる (an older verb meaning "to crouch low to the ground"). Always intransitive.

USAGE:
- Literal: getting down flat on hands and knees (to search, to take cover, to crawl)
- Figurative: behaving abjectly, groveling, or being utterly humbled

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{這|は}いつくばる: to flatten oneself on the floor
- ⟦{地面|じめん}→地面：00125_jimen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{這|は}いつくばる: to lie prone on the ground
- {這|は}いつくばって⟦{謝|あやま}る→謝る：01177_ayamaru⟧: to prostrate oneself in apology
- {這|は}いつくばってで⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧: even if I have to grovel (set emphatic phrase)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ひれ{伏|ふ}す: to prostrate oneself — more formal/literary; emphasizes lying face-down out of reverence or submission
- ⟦{土下座|どげざ}→土下座：17393_dogeza⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to bow on one's knees with forehead to the ground — a specific ritualized posture of apology
